newsitem.title: USA: Viacom has higher third quarter on strength of units.
newsitem.headline: Viacom has higher third quarter on strength of units.

text.p: Entertainment giant Viacom Inc. Friday reported higher third quarter results, based on the strength of its MTV Networks, Paramount studios and Blockbuster video store results.
"At Blockbuster, we continue to generate strong revenue growth as we expand both domestically and in key territories abroad," Chairman Sumner Redstone said in a statement.
"We are confident that we have the right management team and the right strategic blueprint" to enhance earnings and revenues in the coming year.
Viacom reported third quarter earnings of $102 million, or 27 cents a share, compared with $78 million, or 17 cents a share, in the year-earlier period.
Revenues in the third quarter rose to $3.35 billion from $2.95 billion a year earlier.
In particular, the performance at MTV Networks was outstanding, Redstone said, with 27 percent gains in both revenues and EBITDA, or earnings before income taxes, depreciation and other charges.
Paramount also delivered higher revenues and operating results in both its motion picture and television operations, he said.
It said Paramount's third quarter gains reflect increased feature motion picture sales to television networks and a rise in cable and syndication revenues of the television programming library.
Higher results at Paramount were aided by the box office popularity of the recent films "Mission Impossible," "The First Wives Club," and "Primal Fear."
Viacom said its MTV Networks third quarter revenues of $349 million increased by 27 percent, mostly from double-digit gains in affiliate fees and advertising sales.
Separately, Redstone Thursday accused Seagram Co. Ltd. Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. of trying to disrupt the companies' joint venture cable partnership by taking legal action against Viacom.

In his second day on the witness stand in Delaware Chancery Court, Redstone said Bronfman had assured him in March that Seagram would not sue Viacom over the launch of Viacom's new cable channel "Nick at Nite TV Land."
Canadian beverage firm Seagram filed suit in April, however, prompting Redstone to accuse Bronfman of trying to destroy the companies' USA Networks venture.
Viacom and Seagram, which also owns entertainment and theme park concern MCA Inc., have been fighting for control of the cable partership.
Viacom stock was up 75 cents at $33.375 in morning trading on the American Stock Exchange.
